channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Candidates vying for Nebraska House seat face off in debate
item.description: The candidates in a competitive U.S. House race in Nebraska faced off in a debate. The winner would replace retiring GOP Rep. Don Bacon.

item.description: How does President Trump's travel compare to past campaigns and what does it say about Republicans' level of concern about the midterms?

item.title: What the GOP's money moves suggest about the party's midterm outlook
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with political analyst Ron Brownstein about recent shifts in GOP spending and messaging, and what they suggest about how the party views its chances in the midterms.

item.description: Trump's campaign tour continues as Republicans rally voters ahead of midterms, Ukraine faces limited access to Starshield technology, Houthi rebels hit Saudi oil company building.

item.title: LA fire survivors face another setback with FEMA program delays
item.description: The fight over a FEMA program aiding some of LA's most vulnerable wildfire victims is the latest setback for hundreds of fire survivors who still haven't rebuilt after the deadly 2025 infernos.

item.title: Group that plants fruit trees in vacant lots grows to cities nationwide
item.description: A Kansas City group set up to help volunteers plant fruit trees in vacant city lots has quickly branched out across the country with almost 850 orchards in 17 cities with more to come.

item.description: The latest tough inflation report reinforces the challenge for President Trump and GOP candidates ahead into the midterm elections.

item.title: Social Security could soon run out of money. Here are some possible solutions
item.description: Social Security may run short of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. The team from NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.

item.title: Wyoming tribes ask church pastor to leave after viral sermon
item.description: Tribes on the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming are asking a Christian pastor to leave after she denigrated their native religion in a sermon.

item.title: France investigates cyberattack that hacked retailers' refrigeration systems
item.description: France has opened an investigation into a cyberattack that hit hundreds of food retailers, causing refrigerators to malfunction across the country.
